propositions: Blocking edges written before comparability became structural remain invalid on disk because LINK events are durable and not re-resolved on read, causing epics to appear blocked by their own children and distorting ready/next-batch scheduling.

The doctor command scans net-active blocking edges against the current resolver to classify findings into three kinds: ancestor-blocking (endpoint is ancestor of other), mis-escalated (resolver returns different pair), and unreadable (endpoint cannot be reduced).

The --repair flag writes replacement links before removing stale edges so interruption leaves a superset the next run converges; it declines repairs where an UNLINK would cancel a different relation (ambiguous-pair) and refuses to run while a reconciler pass is in flight.

On the repository's own tracker, 18 bad edges were found (9 ancestor-blocking, 9 mis-escalated); 12 were repaired; 8 residuals have closed blocked sides and cannot affect scheduling because closed tickets never appear in ready or next-batch.

The run_repair initial design held the tracker write lock across its loop, causing it to self-deadlock (60s timeout on every inner write); the fix drops the outer lock since atomicity is not required—replacement written before stale unlink provides resumability.

Re-parenting silently invalidates previously-correct edges without touching the link itself, causing new mis-escalated edges with open endpoints to appear post-remediation, making doctor an ongoing check rather than one-shot cleanup.
